rounds.text: Black Box Ltd demonstrates exceptional capital efficiency, evidenced by a 3-year median ROE of 35% [E27] and a trailing ROE of 25.7% [E13], both comfortably exceeding the sector benchmark of 10.41% [E9]. The company shows robust medium-term compounding with 3-year profit growth reaching 80% [E20], supported by expanding operating margins that rose to 9% in TTM from 7% three years earlier [E29]. Market momentum and institutional accumulation strongly validate this performance, as shown by a relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E51], a positive institutional money flow of +1.85 percentage points [E44], and a rules-based screen scoring 85 out of 100 with a medium confidence buy signal [E64]. Conceded: [E45], [E46], [E47], [E70].

Black Box Ltd trades at a highly stretched valuation, with a trailing P/E of 57.3x [E1] that balloons to 72.59x against a sector benchmark of just 20.4x [E6], while its EV/EBITDA of 29.79x heavily outpaces the sector benchmark of 11.25x [E11]. This excessive pricing is completely disconnected from its fundamental delivery; compounded sales growth has stalled to 0% over the last 3 years [E16], and 5-year compounded sales growth sits at a sluggish 6% [E15]. Expectations are running unsustainably ahead of reality, as evidenced by a price-led divergence where 5-year price growth of 36% far outpaces 13% profit growth [E56]. Furthermore, cash generation is alarming: cash conversion stands at a meager 0.39x with operating cash flow making up only 20% of operating profit in March 2026 [E33, E36], while debtor days have worsened significantly from 41.2 to 66.6 days [E63]. A reverse DCF exposes that the current market price of ₹922 already prices in an aggressive 26.0% earnings growth rate [E47], supported by a dangerously low dividend yield of 0.11% [E4] and escalating borrowings that climbed to ₹1,153 Cr in March 2026 [E39]. Conceded: the company displays strong historical return metrics, including a 3-year median ROE of 35% [E27] and robust 3-year compounded profit growth of 80% [E20].

Conceded: [E1], [E6], [E11], [E16], [E33], [E36], [E63]. The bear points to stretched headline multiples and slowing historical sales, but ignores the company's compounding earnings engine, which boasts a 25% 10-year profit growth [E18] and an exceptional 80% compounded profit growth over the last 3 years [E20]. While cash conversion and debtor days require monitoring, the business consistently rewards capital allocation with a robust 3-year median ROE of 35% [E27] and a trailing ROE of 21.34% that comfortably outperforms the sector benchmark of 10.41% [E9]. Conceded: [E4], [E39], [E47]. Despite concerns over dividend yield and rising borrowings, institutional confidence is surging with a positive money flow and a major inflow from domestic institutions leaping from 0.01% to 3.41% [E43, E44]. Furthermore, the rules-based screen awards the company a strong 85 out of 100 score driven by recent fundamental momentum including 24% YoY sales growth and 19% YoY net profit growth [E64, E65, E67], validating the market's high relative-strength rating of 100 [E51] rather than writing it off as mere speculation.

Conceded: [E20], [E27]. The bull highlights rapid profit growth and high return on equity, but ignores the stark reality that historical compounding has completely decoupled from top-line expansion, with 3-year compounded sales growth stagnant at 0% [E16] and 5-year sales growth slipping to a poor 6% [E15, E61]. While domestic institutions increased holdings [E43], this influx fails to mask severe fundamental disconnects: cash conversion reads an alarming 0.39x with operating cash flow making up just 20% of operating profit [E33, E36], accompanied by a sharp deterioration in debtor days from 41.2 to 66.6 days [E63]. Furthermore, relying on recent YoY momentum ignores the glaring valuation risk where today's price demands an unsustainable 26.0% earnings growth against a base case of 13.0% [E47], resulting in an extreme DCF overvaluation of -156.0% [E46, E69]. Finally, the stock trades at massive premiums—including a P/E of 57.3x to 72.59x against a 20.4x sector benchmark [E1, E6] and a P/B of 12.75x against a 2.04x sector benchmark [E7]—leaving the high relative-strength score [E51] completely unsupported by underlying cash generation [E33] or durable revenue expansion [E16].

Conceded: [E16], [E33], [E36], [E63]. While top-line metrics show near-term friction, the business maintains a phenomenal rules-based screen score of 85 out of 100 with a BUY recommendation [E64], driven by robust recent performance including 24% YoY sales growth and 19% YoY net profit growth [E65, E67]. The bear’s valuation concerns ignore exceptional profitability fundamentals, including a 3-year median ROE of 35% [E27] and an average 5-year median ROE of 32% [E26], which significantly outperform the sector benchmark of 10.41% [E9]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is clearly expanding through positive money flow and a 3.40 percentage point increase in domestic institutional holdings [E43, E44], validating the market's willingness to pay a premium. The chart exhibits definitive technical strength with the stock trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a maximum relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E51], proving that strong momentum is fully backed by superior operational returns and accelerating profit growth [E20].

While the bull highlights a high screen score [E64], that same system warns of a -156% margin of safety [E46] and notes that the current price implies 26% earnings growth—double the base case assumption [E47]. The recent 24% YoY sales growth [E65] is undermined by a stagnant 0% compounded sales growth over the last three years [E16] and a poor five-year average of 6.23% [E61]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong median ROE [E27, E59], yet this efficiency is overshadowed by a P/E of 72.59x and a P/B of 12.75x, both of which are massive multiples of their respective sector benchmarks [E6, E7]. Although domestic institutions have increased their stake [E43], overall confidence is mixed as promoters have reduced their holdings [E41] and foreign institutional ownership has also declined [E42]. Technical momentum [E50, E51] appears detached from fundamentals, as price growth has exceeded profit growth by 57% recently [E57], while trailing twelve-month profit growth has slowed to just 4% [E21]. Finally, the quality of reported earnings is compromised by a weak cash conversion ratio of 0.39x [E33], where profits are far ahead of cash, and a sharp increase in debtor days to 66.6 [E63].
